[spoiler=Scholar and Jurist Independence Act][b]Ministry of Religious Affairs[/b]

[u]Grand Majlisi Passes Islamic Scholars and Jurists Independence Act of 2027, Approved by Sultan Masud[/u]

[i]بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم[/i]

After months of discussion and deliberation in the houses of the Grand Majlisi, the Councils of Emirs voted to approve the Islamic Scholars and Jurists Independence Act of 2027 by a vote of 50 in favor and 25 against. This historic piece of legislation formally codifies the generally recognized and respected norm of Islamic scholars and jurists not receiving funding from political parties or the government, but rather from nonprofit organizations called Waqf, or charitable foundations funded by private citizens or apolitical religious, union, or collective organizations. 

In brief, this will make it illegal for Islamic scholars and jurists to: 
A) Belong to any political party or endorse any political party, to avoid any possibility of bias in their rulings and judgements,
B) Makes it illegal for any political party or the government to even partially fund any Waqf organizations
C) Protects scholars and jurists from being politically persecuted or unfairly prosecuted for any basic and non inflammatory criticism of the government or any political figures, even the Sultan
D) Strengthens the role of scholars and jurists as watchdogs and checks on governmental power

In shaa Allah, this will help to avoid the corruption of scholars and jurists by the government or political parties, and keep them accountable to firmly applying the law in their decisions and rulings without favoritism, bribery, or fear of unjust penalties. 

[i]Maryam al-Khalidi
Minister of Religious Affairs[/i][/spoiler]

[quote=hayan_dal;60995508]The borders of Hayan-Dal had been shrunk from the former glorious state. This was a grave transgression against the faithful people of the nation.

General Secretary Jin Taeja grimaced. He had only taken power around two weeks ago, and although he had many plans, there wasnt that much he could do with the current state of the nation. He stood from his desk at the Seong, the highest governmental building in all of Hayan-Dal, and took a walk through the halls. He did this to clear his mind, but it was futile; he just kept thinking of ways to improve the situation of the nation.

He turned left at the hallway intersection and walked past two wooden doors. At the third, he gently rested his hand on its bronze handle. He almost turned back. Taeja turned the knob and entered.

The room he entered had twelve pews, six on each side. He walked on the scarlet carpet stretching from the entryway to the altar. At the front, behind the ornate altar, was a large golden crucifix. Taeja read the inscription at the top of the cross.

[i][pre]    IESUS NAZARENUS REX IUDAEORUM[/pre][/i]

Taeja knelt on one knee before the altar. He held the silver cross that hung around his neck with his right hand, and a few quiet moments passed. Finally, he closed his eyes.

[i]Heavenly Father,[/i] he began, [i]Lord of Hosts. Your name is holy above all others, sanctified in a world of impurity. Only Yours is the glory, and only Yours is the power.[/i]

He paused. [i]God, Ive come to ask you for guidance. I desire to grow the borders of our nation, to build up our strength, and yet there seems to be no good avenue through which it could be done. I need your help, just an idea.[/i]

Taeja looked up from his reflective posture about to speak once more, until the image of the Savior struck him. Taeja had been searching for a worldly solution to solve worldly issues, but he had neglected the answer that lied before him. Taeja forgot, [i]He[/i] is the truth, the solution to the issues anyone would face.

The General Secretary lowered his head once more. [i]I thank You, king of kings. You are wise and powerful beyond measure; I ask that You bestow your power and grace upon me, let me do Your on this earth. In the name of Christ, Amen.[/i]

Taeja stood slowly and in reverence. He tucked the silver cross around his neck beneath his gray shirts collar, turned, and left.

[spoiler=
[pre]Movement from the Heavens[/pre]]

The morning sun sat low on the horizon. Thousands gathered under the Seongs balcony, ready to hear the words of the General Secretary.

Taeja, meanwhile, paced through the halls. He wore a gray commanders outfit: a soldiers coat with decorations pinned onto it on top of a gray shirt and tie, dark gray pants, and black boots. It had been a week since the prayer that inspired him to take this course of action. He would be lying if he said that he wasnt nervous in the slightest bit, but he knew that this was meant to be. Taeja knew he was chosen.

He turned sharply towards the hall that took him to the balcony, and with one grand motion, opened the double wooden doors. At his appearance, the people below cheered.

The General Secretary walked towards the podium prepared and tapped the microphone twice. He waited until the people had quieted down to begin speaking. [i]Greetings, people of Hayan-Dal. It is such a fine morning, I hope you all are well.[/i]

He paused for a short while. [i]I come here to speak to you about a great issue that plagues our nation. That is, the one of faith.[/i] The crowd grew even more quiet and still. Taeja continued. [i]We are silent in a time when this godless world needs to hear the Word. We are isolated when we should be reaching out. We, as a nation, are doing good, but as Gods prophets, we are failing.[/i]

He paused for a little while. [i]This is not a problem without remedy, however. This is something that we can all do to fix this. First, we must initiate programs to help our brothers and sisters who fall behind. I already have drafts of these programs sitting on my desk. Secondly, we increase our industrial capacity. This will give us more wealth and resources, and finally allow us to look outwards with more serious intentions. And then-![/i] He raised his fist. [i]And then, we push our borders! We take more land, dedicating yet another part of this world to God. We must spread the faith, and grow our power. We need to strengthen the nation in order to remain faithful. After all, faith without works is dead. And it is in our best interest to remain alive in Him.[/i]

The people below Taeja cheered loudly. He let their praises lift themselves high to him. Looking over the crows, he couldnt help but smile; this was surely the work of God.

[i]After the nation is ready,[/i] he began again after the cheering had died down, [i]I will assemble a group of some faithful few to help with some tasks related to this. But now, we must remember this: the will of God has set our destiny before us like a fruit hanging from a tree. All we must do is reach forth and pluck the fruit, take our destiny.[/i]

Taeja looked over the crowd as they began to cheer again, and after a few minutes, he turned back into the Seong.
[/spoiler]

[/quote]

General Secretary Taeja had just finished his speech to the nation and had begun to walk back to his office when his religious advisor, Reverend Cheon Haeun, approached him. He was dressed in black clothes decorated with scripture written in golden words.

[i]General Secretary,[/i] he began, [i]that was quite the speech.[/i]

Taeja nodded in acknowledgement. [i]Thank you, Reverend. I try to do my best for this nation. You know that the people need fire in their hearts.[/i]

Reverend Haeun smiled. [i]That is true. Passivity is the snare of the modern age, snatching the youth into fruitless endeavors.[/i]

Taeja nodded again. He resumed his walk to his office as Haeun followed. [i]You know, Reverend, that I have many plans for this nation. We need to expand, thats a need. And, unfortunately, we just dont have the capacity to do it in our current state.[/i]

[i]What is needed to increase our capacity?[/i]

[i]An increase in motivation. We require more missionaries, more soldiers. And with this also comes the demand of the workers that support the systems that allow for us to field these missionaries and soldiers.[/i]

Haeun walked alongside Taeja for a while before nodding his head. [i]I understand, general secretary. I will speak to the leaders of the dioceses and see what can be done.[/i]

The pair had arrived at the door of Taejas office. The General Secretary opened the door slightly and lingered by the entrance.

[i]I appreciate it, Reverend.[/i]

[i]Have you any ideas in particular for what should be preached?[/i]

[i]...I dont have anything concrete, but what I do have are some very general ideas. Importance of the family, importance of missions work, and what it means to be a soldier of Christ. Some topics to give the people something to fight for, and other topics to inspire them to take up arms and fight.[/i]

The Reverend nodded. [i]I will see to it that it is done. I know what plans you want to bring about.[/i]

Taeja nodded in appreciation. [i]Thank you, Reverend.[/i] He began to step inside his office. [i]I will see you at a later date; at this moment I have to work on the logistics on how to mobilize and rally our youth.[/i]

Haeun acknowledged him, and, giving a slight bow, left with no further words. Taeja entered his office, closing the door behind him. He sat at his desk, looking over the paperwork that was prepared for him. The file at the top read:

                        [i][u]First Hayanese Missionary Corp[/u][/i]

He sighed. [i]Well, Ive got to get started somewhere.[/i]

[spoiler=
[u][b]The First Crusade of the Orient[/b][/u]
[pre]
[/pre][i][pre]and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it[/pre][/i][pre]Matthew 16:18[/pre]]

The First Hayanese Missionary Corp was founded by General Secretary Jin Taeja in order to spread the influence of Christendom throughout Erene. It wasnt purely religious: being recognized by the government of Hayan-Dal made it a political tool as well. However, the General Secretary believed this to be necessary. If the Church shied away from entering the sphere of politics, then it would become only partially effective.

The First Crusade of the Orient was declared not as a response to violence against the global kingdom of God, but as a promise to the future generations of Christians that would live on Kianzhou. The continent must be secured as a Christian continent in order to bolster the children of God in the face of spiritual warfare that the world so often ignores.

Thousands of faithful joined the First H.M.S. on its first day of creation. General Secretary Taeja saw to it that they were fitted with the gear necessary for their mission, which was to increase the territory of Hayan-Dal. Money from the national treasury and donations from private corporations helped those who marched on to expand the borders.

General Secretary Taeja led the charge, if it could be called that. In reality, the entire operation was relatively peaceful due to the absence of people in the lands that were taken. The few groups in the way were removed or integrated as they were. The most common method of doing this to the scattered villages was to request they move inwards towards the cities of Hayan-Dal, offering protection and job opportunities. Large settlements that refused were left in peace for the time being, and smaller settlements that refused were forcefully taken inwards.

Upon reaching the coast of Kianzhou, Taeja and the members of the army that accompanied him planted a flag of Hayan-Dal onto the shoreline, showing that this beach now belonged to him. Members of the First H.M.S. celebrated. The clergymen praised the Lord.

The First H.M.S. quickly got to work, turning the vast swaths of land into the territory of Hayan-Dal. Planners and contractors followed behind, quickly scheming the layout for the new territory. Cities were planned in accordance with the natural geography of the area, and prospectors went around to see where the most deposits of natural resources lay.

Eventually, the fire of the First Crusade of the Orient calmed, and the members of the First H.M.S. rallied to hear the General Secretary speak to them. The event lasted six days, and on the seventh, they rested, and listened to the words of their leader.

[i]To all you faithful who have accompanied me on this journey,[/i] Taeja began, [i]I deeply thank. You have my most profound appreciation. This would not be possible without all of you. You have all answered the call of God through the highest office of the government of Hayan-Dal, and your success has proved you all to be full of zeal for our Lord. Once we return to the former borders of our nation, you will be rewarded for your service. It is with the help of those like you that the will of Christ can be done on Erene.[/i]

[i]The lands that we have claimed for ourselves have been in relative disorder. We will bring order. These lands have been faithless. We will bring faith. Every good thing that this land has lacked, we shall provide, and in excess, so that the glory of God can be made clear. And at every opportunity we will lift up the kingdom of God on Erene. Strength, wealth, power of all kinds shall be ours to wield against the forces of darkness of this world.[/i]

[i]Over this past week, we have gained a tremendous victory. This land is what we will use to advance Gods kingdom. However, if we stop at this point, then the efforts we have done will be in vain. For, at the end of the age, our Lord and Savior will not ask us how many acres we have brought to an earthly government, or how much power we have accumulated. No, for it is a vanity of vanities for one to gain the world and lose their soul. Our Lord has spoken about the dangers that arise when we do not do our proper duty and instead eat the fruits that come from our labor as if we are the ones who planted the seeds. We must do something greater. And to do this, we must increase not only our zeal, but also our dedication, and also our knowledge.

It is to the greatest benefit of the kingdom to develop our economy and work force. We must work hard, for nothing good comes easy. It is unreasonable to expect a bad tree to produce good fruit. But the opposite is also true. It is unreasonable to expect a good tree to produce bad fruit. If we are truly working for Christ and submit ourselves to Him, then it is not possible for the fruits of our labor to be insufficient or detrimental to the work of God here in this world.

There is also knowledge. It is futile to work tediously and not know where the money is going. Sure, goods are goods, and services are valuable also, but the nature of many vocations rewards the employer as well, and if the employer is not aligned with the values that Christ would like us to have, then the works of the faithful are unfortunately twisted by the forces of evil. The pursuit of knowledge, with certain limits, is a good one. It would be unbecoming of a faithful individual to donate their income to the church while working in an institution which stands against the church. This is vanity.

I encourage all of you faithful soldiers of Christ to continue to show allegiance through church attendance and using your works to demonstrate your fidelity to our Lord. The Lord of Creation is the one who deserves all of your praise, for He shall make it possible for us to defend ourselves and conquer the spiritual forces of darkness of this world.[/i]

The people applauded him, but the General Secretary bowed and left in humility. He did not want to be the sole focus of the First H.M.S., for he feared becoming an idol to them.

--------
[/spoiler]

The office of the Clerk of the Nation, held by Park Jiwoo, was relatively peaceful in prior times. However, with the plans that the General Secretary had, the man suddenly found himself with a much higher workload. This was not something he protested heavily about, as he did anticipate it and was able to deal with it, though the change was much too abrupt. Jiwoo would have appreciated it if the General Secretary had eased into these changes. 

After the conclusion of the First Crusade of the Orient, Clerk Park Jiwoo awaited the General Secretary in his office, seated on the chair in front of the leaders desk. This was an act that many of the other members of the executive cabinet would have not done, either out of reverence for the General Secretary or out of fear, but the Clerk did not care. Jiwoo was here not because he was preferred, but because he was needed. There was no one as good as him at his job.

Eventually, after around a half hour of waiting, the General Secretary opened the door to his office. He entered, only noticing the Clerk after a few brief moments.

[i]Clerk Park, it is a surprise to see you here.[/i]

He turned around to face the General Secretary. He did not smile, which was not out of the ordinary. [i]Please, have a seat, We have much to discuss.[/i]

General Secretary Taeja complied, sitting at his desk. He shot the Clerk a glare, which was not received.

The Clerk pulled out a briefcase and opened it, removing file after file and placing them on the desk before him. He sorted them into neat piles of seven, and by the end there was a total of six stacks of files, seven files tall.

A brief moment later, Taeja interrupted the silence. [i]I suppose this is about the amount of paperwork that Ive made you do?[/i]

Jiwoo shook his head. [i]No, this is the amount of paperwork that [b]you[/b] have to do. No one else is authorized to do it.[/i]

[i]And what is this for?[/i]

[i]The first stack of files is for the official recognition of the First Hayanese Missionary Corps, and sets the groundwork for additional. I assume you want additional, since you went through the trouble of naming it the [b]first[/b] of these corps. They also try to alleviate the PR crisis that comes with this. Surely you have noticed by now that the Parliament and the Highest Court are more passive than you are. Such a radical creation would be pushed against hard. I expect that its currently the talk of the Highest Court. The Parliament must feel blindsided, as custom dictates that the General Secretary should consult with the Parliament before the creation of any executive bodies.[/i]

[i]...And the others?[/i]

[i]Stacks two to six are regarding some corporations and contractors that want to work with the land. They are divided up based on residential, industrial, military, agrarian, and mining opportunities. I will not delve too deeply into this, as it would be beneficial for you to familiarize yourself with the benefits and detriments of each individual entity that desires business with the new region. The seventh stack regards the official annexation of the region. It is one thing to take it, but it must be recognized. You have the recognition of the people, which would sway the Highest Court and the Parliament given enough time, but in order to sway them now, we need to act.[/i]

The General Secretary sighed and leaned back into his chair. It was painful, but he [b]had[/b] chosen this job for himself.

[i]Very well. Thank you for your help, Clerk Park, you are dismissed.[/i]

Without saying anything, the Clerk closed his briefcase, stood, and then left the room, leaving Taeja to review and sign these documents.

[i]I should get started[/i] he muttered.
